text:
Amanda: Heads up — seeing a spike in structured-output rejections from the output shim in prod for /chat.invoke. Reject rate jumped ~20x after the 2026-03-20 shim rollout :eyes:

Amanda: Example log snippet from edge:```
error=SchemaRejected reason=extra_keys adapter=output-shim route=/chat.invoke model=redwood-v2
payload={"response":{"type":"tool","name":"search","args":{"q":"foo","extra":42}}}
```

Bryan: Is that the strict-schema toggle we enabled in the shim canary? @Leo did we flip soft-validate globally?

Leo: We did not flip it globally. The canary config was scoped to eu-west only. My gut: shim is dropping/rewriting metadata when it converts streaming fncall -> toolcall, so route_id ends up null in the telemetry. When route_id is null the dashboard mapping assigns requests to the degen/fallback route which inflates that route's reject numbers and misattributes quotas.

Maria: That would explain the billing surface spikes customers are seeing. Console currently filters out null route_id rows from the per-route dashboard (we assumed null=internal), so samples are missing. We need to surface nulls as "unknown" and show sample links.

Amanda: Immediate mitigation I propose: 1) rollback shim change in prod, 2) enable 0.5% sampled collection of raw rejected payloads (PII scrubper pipeline), 3) temporary alert: reject_rate(route=/chat.invoke) > 3% for 5m. Thoughts? :warning:

Leo: Agreed on sampling + scrubber. I'll open a small PR to preserve original request metadata across the shim boundary and add a metadata field `validation_stage` with values `pre`/`post` so we can tell where validation failed. Plan: canary patch -> 1% traffic eu-west -> validate samples -> ramp.

Bryan: From a rollout policy perspective: we should prefer soft-validate for 1% canaries, collect telemetry, then hard-validate at 10% if no regression. Also add a special quota tag for validation rejects so billing doesn't get confused.

Maria: Console work items: - add a 'Rejects by reason' heatmap (by route_id) - add an explicit bucket for "unknown route" - add a link on each reject row to a redacted trace sample (opens in S3 viewer)

Amanda: I'll file the incident and tie it to the deploy. If we can't rollback fast, put the shim into permissive mode (coerce extra keys to a subfield) as a stopgap.

sre-bot: Automated alert created: INCIDENT-2026-03120-57 (priority P2) — routing/telemetry mismatch. Pager duty notified.

deploy-bot: Rollback started for service=output-shim revision=rev_2026_03_20_11:12. ETA ~2m.

Leo: Opening PRs: 1) shim: preserve route_id + validation_stage + reject_reason enum, 2) telemetry: tag mapping logic to prefer original route_id over fallback, 3) console: surface null/unknown rows and sample link. Will add unit tests for streaming fncall->toolcall path.

Bryan: Add a dashboard alert: sudden increase in "rejects mapped to unknown route" should trigger before per-route reject alerts so platform ops can catch attribution issues earlier.

Maria: UX note — when we show a sample payload in the console make the redaction rules visible (fields stripped) and a one-click request sample button for SEs with access.

Amanda: Thanks all. Next steps: Leo PRs + quick rollback (in progress) + incident doc. I'll ping infra if rollback has issues. :thumbsup:

Leo: Rolling back pushed; running integration smoke tests now. If green I'll promote the permissive shim patch and add sampling.|
